current_bottleneck: 631a and 638a establish a defensible mixed-coordinate need: IV cells need support-valid level-score generation to prevent explosions and fix tails, while anchor factors need encoded-increment generation to preserve factor changes and joint co-movement. The bottleneck is implementing this as one shared model and preprocessing spec, not as two glued scenario generators.
last_result_summary: 640a audited 631a vs 638a coordinate evidence. For IV, 638a fixed support/tails: explosion 0.0% vs 51.7%, time_series pass, q99 tail pass 22/25 vs 19/25, pathwise q90/q99 0.733/0.896 vs 2.519/6.007, cross-cell corr ratio 0.998 vs 0.939. For anchors, 631a was much better: factor KS mean 0.115 vs 0.156, q99 pass 13/13 vs 6/13, factor-factor gen abs corr 0.133 vs 0.052, IV-factor gen abs corr 0.119 vs 0.073. Conclusion: mixed coordinate is justified as a data-coordinate spec if it remains one model/one rollout.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 641a as a one-model mixed-coordinate transition: level-score deltas for iv:* channels, encoded increments for factor:* channels, same state-conditioned memory, same velocity network, same joint38 rollout. Evaluate whether it preserves 638a IV support/tail gains while recovering 631a-like anchor-factor q99 and joint dependence.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 631a remains the incumbent clean native joint learned base because it has 4/11 IV score and much better joint-panel audit than 638a. 638a is a coordinate milestone for IV stability, not a deployable joint model.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
